subject: Security exhibit: evidence playbook, pen-test sprint plan, and MSA/order-form redline queue
messages:
From: Alexandra Ortiz <a.ortiz@medallionbio.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-07T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Security exhibit and pen test logistics (MSA/Order Form)

Kimberly —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Before we finalize the order form we need to align on a few items in the security exhibit and pen-test language so our InfoSec and procurement teams can sign off. Can you confirm the following?

- Access model for pen tests (staging only vs. scoped production; ephemeral creds vs. shared VPN)
- Typical windowing you can commit to for scheduled pen tests and expected notice period
- Evidence cadence for SOC 2 artifacts (quarterly snapshot vs. on-request samples) and what artifacts you can reasonably provide (Syslog retention, change control, user access lists)
- Do you have a sample order-form clause for limited inspection / audit rights we can review?

I attached our questionnaire (Medallion_SecQ_v2.xlsx) with the team's initial asks. Can we get an initial response by EOD Tuesday? We have an internal compliance review on Wednesday.

Best,
Alexandra Ortiz
Head of Security, Medallion Bio
security@medallionbio.com

Attachment: Medallion_SecQ_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Alexandra Ortiz <a.ortiz@medallionbio.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-07T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit and pen test logistics (MSA/Order Form)

Alexandra —

Thanks for the clear asks and for sending the questionnaire. High-level plan from our side: we want to run two parallel tracks so legal can finish MSA/order form redlines while ops/engineering scope the operational playbook for evidence and pen testing.

Quick answers up front:
- Pen test access: we prefer bounded inspection against a mirrored staging environment with ephemeral credentials for the testing window. Production access is possible only under an approved escalation, with a signed runbook and a one-week notice.
- Notice/window: standard is a 72-hour notice for scheduled staging tests and a 2-week notice if production access is required. We can support a 3–5 business day rolling window for remediation evidence after the test.
- Evidence cadence: we provide quarterly SOC 2 snapshots plus a scoped artifact package on request (logs, config change history, RBAC lists) with a 5 business day turnaround for typical asks. Deep forensic or large exports may need a longer lead time — we'll document exceptions in the playbook.

Next steps I propose (please confirm):
1) Legal redline: Priyom to propose firm language for (a) limited inspection (b) pen-test scope and (c) data handling during tests.
2) Ops runbook: Marcus + Laura to draft a one-page evidence handoff that maps artifact -> owner -> SLA.
3) Customer input: Alexandra to flag any lines in your attached questionnaire that are "deal blockers" (highlighted) so we can prioritize.

I'll attach a short redline summary so the teams have a single reference. Priyom — can you take the lead on option language by tomorrow EOD? Marcus/Laura — can you sketch the evidence-owner table by Friday?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
kp@redwood.com

Attachment: kp-redline-summary.pdf (summary of proposed splits between legal/ops)

From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, Alexandra Ortiz <a.ortiz@medallionbio.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-08T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit and pen test logistics (MSA/Order Form)

Kimberly / Alexandra —

Thanks — I took a pass at firm language for the MSA/order form exhibit and the pen-test clause. Below are two options for the pen-test language (option A = tighter, option B = more permissive). Please indicate which you prefer; we can insert the chosen text into the order form and run a single redline back to Medallion procurement.

Option A (bounded inspection, staging-first):
"Customer may conduct security testing against Redwood's designated staging environment only, with no access to production systems or production data. Redwood will provide ephemeral credentials scoped to the testing window and a named point-of-contact. Customer must provide no less than 72 hours' notice and provide a test plan for Redwood review. Any request for production access must be separately agreed in writing and is subject to Redwood's change-control and operational gating."

Option B (production-with-controls):
"Customer may request production testing subject to mutually agreed controls. Redwood may require a documented runbook, a remediation escrow agreement, and a minimum of 10 business days' notice. Production testing may be conditional on a dedicated engineering window and may incur a professional services fee."

Audit / Inspection (recommended clause for order form exhibit):
"Redwood will make reasonably necessary personnel and technical artifacts available for Customer's compliance review in accordance with the following: (i) quarterly SOC 2 reports (Type II) where available; (ii) a scoped artifact package on written request with a 5 business day SLA for common artifacts (audit logs, access lists, change history); and (iii) an agreed-upon evidence cadence for deeper artifacts requiring additional time. Audit activities shall be limited to a role-based scope and not include live tampering of production data without express prior approval."

Operational notes / asks from our side:
- Please confirm whether Medallion requires production access for the initial testing cycle (Y/N). If yes, specify the types of tests that require production (auth bypass, data exfiltration, etc.).
- If you prefer Option B, we'll draft a short professional-services statement for the order form.

I've attached two files: proposed-pen-test-clause.txt (text you can paste into the order form) and evidence-cadence-sla.csv (a sample SLA table mapping artifacts -> owner -> turnaround). Marcus/Laura — FYI, Priyom wants the owner table validated against ops reality.

Happy to hop on a 30-min call if that would speed sign-off.

--
Priyom Das
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed-pen-test-clause.txt, evidence-cadence-sla.csv

From: Alexandra Ortiz <a.ortiz@medallionbio.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-09T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit and pen test logistics (MSA/Order Form)

Thanks Priyom, Kimberly —

We reviewed Option A and prefer the bounded inspection / staging-first model. Medallion does not require production access for the initial engagement. A couple of quick items:

- Can Redwood commit to the 72-hour notice for staging tests? (Yes/No)
- We accept the 5 business day SLA for the scoped artifact package; for anything that needs more time we'll surface it as an "extended artifact" request and expect a timeline.
- Please go ahead and insert the Option A wording into the order form and route for signature. We will need a redline by EOD Monday so our procurement queue can pick it up.

I’ve attached a short PoC Order Form detail sheet (PoC-orderform-details.pdf) that lists the test objectives and responsible Medallion contacts. Once Redwood confirms the redline insertion, we will push a DocuSign package (link below) and start scheduling the staging window — target week of Apr 19.

DocuSign (placeholder): https://docusign.com/ABC-DEF-ghi-1234

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

Alexandra Ortiz
Head of Security, Medallion Bio

Attachment: PoC-orderform-details.pdf (PDF)
